name: foreach-fanout
notes: The `foreach` grammar (ADR-0039): one template subgraph, instantiated once per declared key, so 'one node per symbol' stops being N hand-copied nodes. The document STORES this section (it is identity — adding a key is a different computation) and DERIVES what runs; nothing here is a template language, only fan-out over a key list. Run it: python -m dskit.pipeline run examples/pipeline/foreach-fanout.json --asof 2026-01-01

foreach.notes: The two synthetic instruments. Keys are a SET — declared in any order, sorted at construction — and each one names the instances it builds: template `rows` becomes rows__syna and rows__synb (node keys take the key's slug; `$each` substitutes the RAW key). Add a third instrument by adding a key here, and nothing else.

rows.notes: `$each` is substituted as a WHOLE value only — never interpolated into a longer string, which is the line between fan-out and templating. The `$dataset.events` wire names a SHARED node, so it rides through unrewritten; a reference to another TEMPLATE key would be re-aimed at that template's instance for this key.

dataset.notes: role 'data': the shared deterministic source every instance filters. Shared nodes are declared here, once.

params.provenance_waiver: one synthetic source, fanned out per instrument — the ports are the instruments, not two venues

both.notes: Port fan-out is OPT-IN: a port written '<base>__each' whose reference names a template key becomes one port per key (records__syna, records__synb). Nothing is fanned out automatically — a Node declares no port set, so the engine cannot know which ports are fannable.
